ja: 太陽の表面温度は約5500℃だが、外側の大気（コロナ）は100万℃以上になる。その理由はまだ完全には解明されていない。
easy: The surface of the sun is about 5,500°C. But the air around it is over one million degrees. Scientists still do not fully know why.
std: The Sun's surface is about 5,500°C, yet its outer atmosphere, the corona, exceeds a million degrees. Why the corona is so much hotter is still not fully understood.

ja: 光が太陽から地球に届くまで約8分20秒かかる。今見えている太陽は約8分前の姿。
easy: Light from the sun takes about eight minutes to reach us. So the sun we see is the sun of eight minutes ago.
std: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, so we always see the Sun as it was a little over eight minutes earlier.

ja: 観測できる宇宙には数千億〜2兆個の銀河があると推定されている。天の川銀河だけでも1000億〜4000億個の星がある。
easy: There may be hundreds of billions of groups of stars in space. Our own group has more than 100 billion stars.
std: Estimates suggest the observable universe holds hundreds of billions, perhaps up to two trillion, galaxies. The Milky Way alone contains 100 to 400 billion stars.

ja: 土星の平均密度は水より低い。理屈の上では、土星が入るほど巨大な海があれば浮かぶ。
easy: Saturn is lighter than water for its size. If there were a sea big enough, Saturn could float in it.
std: Saturn's average density is lower than that of water, so in theory it would float in an ocean large enough to hold it.

ja: 月は毎年約3.8cmずつ地球から遠ざかっている。数億年後には皆既日食が起きなくなると考えられている。
easy: The moon moves about 3.8 cm away from us every year. In a few hundred million years, it will be too far to fully cover the sun.
std: The Moon drifts about 3.8 cm farther from Earth each year. In several hundred million years it will appear too small to cause total solar eclipses.

ja: 木星の大赤斑は地球より大きな巨大な嵐で、少なくとも150年以上観測され続けている。
easy: Jupiter has a giant storm that is bigger than the Earth. People have watched it for more than 150 years.
std: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth that has been observed continuously for more than 150 years.

ja: 宇宙の年齢は約138億年。地球の年齢（約46億年）の約3倍にあたる。
easy: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old. That is about three times as old as the Earth.
std: The universe is roughly 13.8 billion years old, about three times the age of Earth, which formed around 4.6 billion years ago.

ja: 中性子星は太陽より重い質量を直径20km程度に押し込めた星。ティースプーン1杯分で約10億トンになる。
easy: A neutron star is heavier than the sun but only about 20 km wide. One small spoon of it would weigh about a billion tons.
std: A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere about 20 km across. A teaspoon of its material would weigh around a billion tons.

ja: 金星の1日（自転にかかる243日）は1年（公転225日）より長い。しかも金星では太陽が西から昇る。
easy: On Venus, one day is longer than one year. And the sun comes up in the west.
std: Venus takes 243 Earth days to spin once but only 225 to orbit the Sun, so its day is longer than its year. It also spins backward, so the Sun rises in the west.

ja: 国際宇宙ステーション（ISS）は約90分で地球を1周するため、1日に16回ほど日の出と日の入りを見られる。
easy: The space station goes around the Earth in about 90 minutes. People on it can see about 16 sunrises a day.
std: The International Space Station circles Earth roughly every 90 minutes, so its crew sees about 16 sunrises and sunsets every day.

ja: ダイヤモンドも鉛筆の芯（黒鉛）も同じ炭素でできている。違うのは原子の並び方だけ。
easy: Diamonds and pencil lead are both made of carbon. The only difference is how the tiny parts are lined up.
std: Diamond and the graphite in pencils are both pure carbon. They differ only in how their atoms are arranged.

ja: 雪の結晶は、まったく同じ形のものはまずないと考えられている。成長中の温度や湿度のわずかな違いで形が変わるため。
easy: It is very likely that no two snowflakes are the same. Small changes in the air change their shape as they grow.
std: It is extremely unlikely for two snowflakes to be identical, because tiny differences in temperature and humidity shape each crystal as it grows.

ja: 虹は本当は円の形をしているが、地面にさえぎられて半円に見える。飛行機から見ると丸い虹が見えることがある。
easy: A rainbow is really a full circle. We only see half because the ground is in the way. From a plane, you can sometimes see the whole circle.
std: Rainbows are actually full circles; the ground hides the lower half. From an aircraft you can sometimes see a complete circular rainbow.

ja: 雷の通り道は約3万℃近くになり、太陽の表面の約5倍熱い。ただしその熱はほんの一瞬しか続かない。
easy: Lightning can be about five times hotter than the surface of the sun. But the heat lasts for only a moment.
std: A lightning channel can reach nearly 30,000°C, about five times hotter than the Sun's surface, but only for a fraction of a second.

ja: 鳥や魚、昆虫の中には地球の磁場を使って方角を知るものがいる。その感じ取る仕組みは完全には解明されていない。
easy: Some birds, fish and insects use the Earth's magnetic field to find their way. We still do not fully know how they feel it.
std: Many birds, fish and insects navigate using Earth's magnetic field, but exactly how they sense it is still not fully understood.

ja: 「シュレーディンガーの猫」は、量子の世界の不思議さを示すための思考実験。箱を開けるまで猫の状態が決まらないという話で有名。
easy: Schrödinger's cat is a famous story about a cat in a box. It shows how strange the world of very small things can be.
std: Schrödinger's cat is a thought experiment about a cat in a sealed box, created to show how strange quantum mechanics seems when applied to everyday objects.

ja: 絶対零度（−273.15℃）は理論上の最低温度。物質はこれ以上冷やせず、分子の動きは最も小さい状態になる。
easy: The lowest possible temperature is minus 273.15°C. Nothing can be colder than this.
std: Absolute zero, minus 273.15°C, is the lowest temperature possible. At this point particles have the least motion that physics allows.

ja: 光の速さ（秒速約30万km）は、宇宙で情報や物が進める最高の速さとされる（特殊相対性理論）。
easy: Light moves about 300,000 km in one second. Nothing can travel faster than light.
std: Light travels about 300,000 km per second, and according to special relativity nothing that carries information can go faster.

ja: 地球は完全な球ではなく、少しつぶれた形をしている。赤道の半径は北極・南極までの半径より約21km長い。
easy: The Earth is not a perfect ball. It is a little wider around the middle, by about 21 km.
std: Earth is not a perfect sphere but slightly flattened; its radius at the equator is about 21 km longer than at the poles.

ja: 太陽は毎秒約6億トンの水素をヘリウムに変えている。この核融合が光と熱を生み出す。
easy: Every second, the sun changes about 600 million tons of one gas into another. This gives us light and heat.
std: Every second the Sun fuses about 600 million tonnes of hydrogen into helium, and this nuclear fusion produces its light and heat.

ja: 流れ星の正体は、砂粒ほどの小さなちり。大気に飛び込んで高温になり、光りながら燃えつきる。
easy: A shooting star is often just a small piece of dust. It burns up as it falls into the air around the Earth.
std: Most shooting stars are specks of dust no bigger than a grain of sand that burn up as they plunge into Earth's atmosphere.

ja: 水は凍ると液体のときより軽くなる（密度が下がる）めずらしい物質。だから氷は水に浮き、湖は底まで凍りにくい。
easy: Ice is lighter than water, which is very unusual. That is why ice floats and lakes do not freeze all the way down.
std: Unusually, water becomes less dense when it freezes. That is why ice floats and why lakes rarely freeze solid from top to bottom.

ja: 水が100℃で沸騰するのは海面の高さでの話。エベレストの山頂では約70℃で沸騰する。
easy: Water boils at 100°C near the sea. On top of Mount Everest, it boils at about 70°C.
std: Water boils at 100°C only at sea level. At the summit of Mount Everest, where the air pressure is low, it boils at about 70°C.

ja: 空気にも重さがある。1立方メートルの空気は約1.2kgで、ふつうの部屋の空気は大人1人分くらいの重さになる。
easy: Air has weight. The air in a normal room can weigh about as much as one adult.
std: Air has weight: one cubic meter weighs about 1.2 kg, so the air in an ordinary room can weigh as much as an adult person.

ja: タコには心臓が3つあり、血は青い。銅を含むヘモシアニンという物質が酸素を運ぶため。
easy: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.
std: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood, because its oxygen is carried by a copper-based protein called hemocyanin.

ja: チーターは時速100kmを超える速さで走れるが、全力で走れるのは数十秒ほど。
easy: A cheetah can run faster than 100 km an hour. But it can only run that fast for a short time.
std: Cheetahs can sprint at over 100 km per hour, but only for a short burst of a few hundred meters.

ja: フラミンゴのひなは灰色っぽい白で生まれる。エサに含まれるカロテノイドという色素で、だんだんピンクになる。
easy: Baby flamingos are not pink. They become pink from the food they eat.
std: Flamingo chicks hatch grey-white. They turn pink gradually thanks to carotenoid pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat.

ja: ゾウはジャンプができない。体が重く脚の作りの関係で、4本の脚が同時に地面から離れることがない。
easy: Elephants cannot jump. They are too heavy, and they always keep at least one foot on the ground.
std: Elephants cannot jump. Because of their weight and leg structure, they always keep at least one foot on the ground, even when moving fast.

ja: ハチの巣の六角形は、少ない材料で広い空間を作れる効率のよい形。数学的にも最も効率がよいことが証明されている。
easy: Bees build their homes with six-sided rooms. This shape uses the least material to make the most space.
std: The hexagons of a honeycomb divide space using the least amount of wall material, something mathematicians proved in 1999.

ja: カメレオンは左右の目を別々に動かせて、ほぼ360度を見渡せる。体の色は、気分や温度、仲間への合図で変わる。
easy: A chameleon can move each eye on its own and see almost all around. Its color changes with its mood and the temperature.
std: A chameleon can move each eye independently to see nearly all around it. Its color shifts mainly with mood, temperature and signals to other chameleons.

ja: サメの骨格は骨ではなく軟骨でできているため、化石に残りにくい。そのかわり歯の化石はたくさん見つかっている。
easy: A shark's body is not held up by hard bone. So shark bodies rarely last as fossils, but many of their teeth do.
std: Shark skeletons are made of cartilage rather than bone, so they seldom fossilize, while their teeth are found in huge numbers.

ja: アリは自分の体重の何十倍もの重さを運ぶことができる。
easy: An ant can carry things many times heavier than its own body.
std: Ants can carry loads many times their own body weight, sometimes up to around fifty times.

ja: クジラの低い鳴き声は、海の中を数千kmも伝わることがある。
easy: The low calls of some whales can travel thousands of kilometers under the sea.
std: The low-frequency calls of large whales such as blue and fin whales can travel thousands of kilometers through the ocean.

ja: カラスは人の顔を見分けて覚えられる。いやなことをした人を何年も覚えていて、仲間にも伝えることがある。
easy: Crows can remember human faces. They can remember a bad person for years and even tell other crows.
std: Crows can recognize individual human faces, remember people who threatened them for years, and even pass the warning to other crows.

ja: 猫のひげは周りを感じ取るセンサー。すき間を通れるかを判断したり、暗い所で動いたりするのに役立つ。
easy: A cat uses its whiskers to feel the world. They help it know if it can fit through a small space.
std: A cat's whiskers are sensitive touch sensors that help it judge narrow gaps and move around in the dark.

ja: 地球には約3兆本の木があると推定されている。人間1人あたり約400本にあたる。
easy: There are about three trillion trees on the Earth. That is about 400 trees for each person.
std: Researchers estimate there are about three trillion trees on Earth, roughly 400 for every person.

ja: カタツムリには歯があり、種類によっては舌の上に何万本もの小さな歯が並んでいる。やすりのように食べ物を削る。
easy: Snails have teeth. Some have thousands of very small teeth on their tongue.
std: Snails have a tongue-like ribbon covered in rows of tiny teeth, called a radula; some species have many thousands of them.

ja: ライオンのたてがみが黒っぽいほど、オスとして強いしるしになり、メスに好まれるという研究がある。
easy: A study found that female lions like males with darker hair around the head.
std: Research in Tanzania found that lions with darker manes tend to be healthier and are preferred by females.

ja: ペンギンは空を飛べないが、水中では時速30km以上で泳げる種類もいる。翼がひれのように進化した。
easy: Penguins cannot fly, but some can swim more than 30 km an hour. Their wings work like flippers.
std: Penguins cannot fly, but their wings have evolved into flippers, and some species can swim at over 30 km per hour.

ja: アイスランドガイという二枚貝には500年以上生きた個体が見つかっている。知られている中で最も長生きの動物のひとつ。
easy: A kind of sea animal with a shell was found to be over 500 years old.
std: An ocean quahog clam found off Iceland was more than 500 years old, making it one of the longest-lived animals ever recorded.

ja: チョウの幼虫はさなぎの中で体の大部分がどろどろに溶け、残った細胞のかたまりから新しい体が作られる。
easy: Inside the hard case, much of a young butterfly's body turns to liquid. Then a new body is built.
std: Inside the chrysalis, much of a caterpillar's body breaks down into a soup, and small groups of cells then build the adult butterfly.

ja: イルカは鏡に映った自分を自分だと分かる。この能力が確かめられている動物は、ヒト・大型類人猿・ゾウなど、ごくわずか。
easy: Dolphins know themselves in a mirror. Very few animals can do this.
std: Dolphins can recognize themselves in a mirror, an ability shown in only a few animals, such as humans, great apes and elephants.

ja: 深海の生き物の多くは自分で光を出す（生物発光）。仲間との合図、えさを誘う、身を守るなどに使う。
easy: Many animals deep in the sea make their own light. They use it to talk, to catch food and to stay safe.
std: Many deep-sea creatures produce their own light, using bioluminescence to signal, attract prey and defend themselves.

ja: ミツバチ1匹が一生のうちに作るハチミツは、ティースプーンの12分の1ほど。
easy: In its whole life, one bee makes only a very small amount of honey, about one twelfth of a small spoon.
std: A single worker honeybee produces only about one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its entire life.

ja: 植物は、干ばつなどのストレスを経験すると、次のストレスにすばやく反応するようになることがある。「植物の記憶」として研究されている。
easy: Some plants seem to remember dry times. After one dry time, they get ready faster for the next.
std: Some plants that survive drought respond faster to the next one, a phenomenon researchers study as 'plant stress memory'.

ja: ナマケモノは動きがとてもゆっくりなので、毛に藻が生え、そこにガが住むこともある。
easy: Sloths move so slowly that green plants grow in their hair. Small insects even live there.
std: Sloths move so slowly that algae grow in their fur, and moths live there too, forming a tiny ecosystem.

ja: ワニの仲間は恐竜の時代から続く古いグループで、体のつくりは大昔からあまり変わっていない。
easy: Crocodiles lived at the same time as dinosaurs. Their bodies have not changed much since then.
std: Crocodilians are an ancient group that lived alongside the dinosaurs, and their basic body plan has changed little since then.

ja: オウムの中には、言葉をまねるだけでなく、色や数を答えるなど意味を理解して使える個体もいた。
easy: Some parrots do more than copy words. One parrot could name colors and count objects.
std: Some parrots do more than mimic: a grey parrot named Alex could name colors, shapes and numbers of objects.

ja: タコは眠っている間に体の色が変わることが観察されていて、夢のような状態があるのではないかと考えられている。
easy: An octopus can change color while it sleeps. Some scientists think it may be dreaming.
std: Sleeping octopuses have been filmed changing color, and some scientists think they may experience something like dreaming.

ja: アメリカの「パンド」は、根でつながった1本のポプラの仲間の群れ。何千年も生きている、地球最古級の生物のひとつ。
easy: Pando is a big group of trees in the United States. All the trees share one root and it is thousands of years old.
std: Pando, a grove of quaking aspen in Utah, is a single organism connected by one root system and is thought to be thousands of years old.

ja: エジプトでピラミッドが作られていたころ、北極海の島ではまだマンモスが生きていた。
easy: When the pyramids were being built in Egypt, some mammoths were still alive on an island in the far north.
std: When the Great Pyramid was built in Egypt, woolly mammoths still survived on Wrangel Island in the Arctic Ocean.

ja: クレオパトラは、ピラミッドが作られた時代よりも、人類が月に行った時代のほうに近い時代の人。
easy: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
std: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.

ja: バイキングはコロンブスより約500年早く北アメリカに着いていた。カナダのランス・オ・メドーに遺跡が残る。
easy: The Vikings reached North America about 500 years before Columbus.
std: Norse explorers reached North America around the year 1000, about 500 years before Columbus, as the site at L'Anse aux Meadows in Canada shows.

ja: モンゴル帝国は最大で約2400万km²を支配した、歴史上最大の陸続きの帝国。
easy: The Mongol Empire was the biggest land empire in history.
std: At its height, the Mongol Empire covered about 24 million square kilometers, the largest connected land empire in history.

ja: ナポレオンの身長は約169cmで、当時のフランス人の平均よりやや高かった。「小柄」というイメージはイギリスの風刺画の影響が大きい。
easy: Napoleon was about 169 cm tall. That was a little taller than most French men at the time.
std: Napoleon was about 169 cm tall, slightly above the average for Frenchmen of his day; his 'short' image owes much to British cartoons.

ja: コロンブスが1492年に最初に着いたのはアメリカ大陸ではなく、バハマ諸島の島だった。
easy: In 1492, Columbus did not land on the big land of America. He landed on a small island in the Bahamas.
std: On his first voyage in 1492, Columbus landed not on the American mainland but on an island in the Bahamas.

ja: 江戸時代は約260年続き、大きな戦争のない時代が長く続いた。その間に日本独自の文化が育った。
easy: The Edo period in Japan lasted about 260 years with no big wars. Many arts grew during that time.
std: Japan's Edo period lasted about 260 years with no major wars, allowing a distinctive culture of art, theater and literature to flourish.

ja: チョコレートの元になるカカオは、16世紀にスペイン人がアメリカ大陸から持ち帰るまでヨーロッパにはなかった。
easy: There was no chocolate in Europe until the Spanish brought it from America in the 1500s.
std: Chocolate was unknown in Europe until Spanish explorers brought cacao back from the Americas in the 16th century.

ja: モナ・リザは、ルーブル美術館に展示される前、フランス王フランソワ1世の宮殿の浴室に飾られていた。
easy: Before it went to a museum, the Mona Lisa hung in a king's bathroom.
std: Before entering the Louvre, the Mona Lisa hung in the bathing rooms of King Francis I's palace at Fontainebleau.

ja: 古代ギリシャのオリンピック（紀元前776年〜）では、選手は裸で競技していた。
easy: In the first Olympic Games in Greece, the players took part with no clothes on.
std: In the ancient Olympic Games, which began in 776 BC, athletes competed naked.

ja: マリー・キュリーはノーベル賞を2回（物理学賞と化学賞）受けた最初の人。異なる2つの科学分野で受賞したのは今も彼女だけ。
easy: Marie Curie was the first person to win the Nobel Prize two times.
std: Marie Curie was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, and she remains the only person honored in two different sciences, physics and chemistry.

ja: グーテンベルクが活版印刷を発明した1440年代、日本は室町時代だった。
easy: When Gutenberg made his printing machine in the 1440s, Japan was in the Muromachi period.
std: When Gutenberg developed his printing press in the 1440s, Japan was in the Muromachi period.

ja: パスポートが広く必要になったのは第一次世界大戦のころから。それ以前は、多くの国境を書類なしで越えられた。
easy: Before the First World War, people could often cross borders without a passport.
std: Passports became widely required only around the First World War; before that, many borders could be crossed without papers.

ja: 1969年のアポロ11号の月面着陸のとき、管制室のスタッフの平均年齢は28歳ほどだったといわれる。
easy: When people first walked on the moon, the team in the control room was very young, about 28 on average.
std: During the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969, the average age of the mission control team is said to have been about 28.

ja: 第一次世界大戦は「クリスマスまでに終わる」と言われていたが、4年以上続き、1500万人以上が亡くなった。
easy: People said the First World War would end by Christmas. It lasted more than four years.
std: Many expected the First World War to be over by Christmas, but it lasted more than four years and killed over 15 million people.

ja: 縄文土器は1万5千年以上前にさかのぼり、世界でも最も古い土器のひとつ。
easy: Some of the oldest pots in the world were made in Japan more than 15,000 years ago.
std: Jōmon pottery from Japan dates back more than 15,000 years, making it among the oldest pottery in the world.

ja: 日本は元号（令和など）を今も公式に使っている唯一の国。最初の元号「大化」は645年で、約1400年の歴史がある。
easy: Japan is the only country that still uses era names, like Reiwa. The first one began in the year 645.
std: Japan is the only country still officially using era names such as Reiwa. The first, Taika, began in 645, nearly 1,400 years ago.

ja: アメリカ独立宣言とアダム・スミスの『国富論』は、どちらも1776年に出た。
easy: The American Declaration of Independence and Adam Smith's famous book came out in the same year, 1776.
std: The US Declaration of Independence and Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations were both published in 1776.

ja: ヴェルサイユ宮殿のぜいたくな建設と維持の費用は、フランスの財政を苦しめた理由のひとつと言われる。
easy: Building the great palace of Versailles cost so much money that it hurt France's economy.
std: The huge cost of building and running the Palace of Versailles is often cited as one strain on French finances before the Revolution.

ja: 古代エジプトでは猫が大切にされ、飼い猫が死ぬと家族がまゆ毛をそって悲しみを表したと伝えられる。
easy: In old Egypt, cats were very special. When a cat died, the family cut off their eyebrows to show they were sad.
std: In ancient Egypt cats were highly respected; according to Herodotus, families shaved their eyebrows in mourning when a pet cat died.

ja: 古代ローマでは鉛を使った水道管や容器が広く使われ、人々が鉛中毒になっていたという説がある。
easy: People in old Rome used a lot of lead. Some people think this made them sick.
std: Ancient Romans used lead widely in pipes and cookware, and some historians suggest lead poisoning harmed public health.

ja: 眼鏡は13世紀のイタリアで発明された。
easy: Glasses for the eyes were first made in Italy in the 1200s.
std: Eyeglasses were invented in Italy in the late 13th century.

ja: 明治維新（1868年）から1945年まではわずか77年。そのあいだに日本は急速に近代化した。
easy: Japan changed very quickly in only 77 years, from 1868 to 1945.
std: Only 77 years passed between the Meiji Restoration in 1868 and 1945, a period of remarkably rapid modernization for Japan.

ja: 最古級の文字「楔形文字」は約5000年前のメソポタミア（今のイラク）で生まれた。最初は物の数の記録に使われた。
easy: One of the first kinds of writing began about 5,000 years ago in what is now Iraq. It was first used to count goods.
std: Cuneiform, one of the earliest writing systems, appeared in Mesopotamia, now Iraq, about 5,000 years ago and was first used to keep records of goods.
